title: Ninth Ward musicians and crossing the river for jobs
summary: Barnes names musicians from downriver and the Ninth Ward, including a valve trombonist, guitar players and Joe Hoodoo, and mentions crossing to jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, no. Those are bad people. What about the Ninth Ward? How many musicians did they have around the Ninth Ward in those times? Well, Henry Ford, he was from down there, wasn't he?
He had one building from the North Coast.
Well, and Vowl, I thought he was from. Yeah.
Well, we had a Vowl Trimole down there, it was called Coon. Called what? Coon. Coon, huh? Joe Hoodoo. What did Joe Hoodoo play? Trimole. Then we had Big Monroe. We had Louis Gould, a guitar player.

No. All his friends passed away. Now we got Freddie Gould, brothers and Louis, who's a guitar player. Then we got another fellow called Ike. He's a guitar player. Let's see who else. That's when Joe DeWasson was coming, during his time, Joe DeWasson was coming up. The clarinet player? Yeah. Was he from down there? He was from down there. He was from down there. He was from the Meta Bell School.
Well, Sheik lives down there now, though.
Sheik, no. Sheik, I told him, she can't eat anything. I must have been a baby. Couldn't have been born there. And who else?
Well, let me ask you about Joe Hoodoo then. What did they call him that?
Wild Nickname. Yeah. No, I couldn't take a dude right now. I know them man's as good as I know Joe.
Well, did he believe in Hoodoo?
No, just kidding, right, you know.

Just a job, that's all. Damping down with tones and going to Damping down to country over the river. Across over river, you had to go to- How do you call this first again? Cut-off. Mm-hm. We crossed the line in the Skip. was getting the skits and going across.
